name: 01_cpu_pipeline
title: A. RV32IM pipeline — 28 continuous clk_sys cycles
subtitle: Reset, forwarding, read wait, taken / not-taken branch, squash, MUL, MMIO and byte store. Selected control assumptions: see README.

rows.name: reset
rows.explanation: Active-high internal CPU reset. Establishes PC=0 and bubbles; reset_n = NOT reset. P1/P2.

rows.name: fetch_pc [31:0]
rows.explanation: Instruction BRAM address, not IF/ID instruction PC. Holds on read wait; redirects to 64 after H. P1.

rows.name: IF + ID instruction
rows.explanation: Returned instruction decoded now; fetch PC is one column ahead. × marks wrong-path work.

rows.name: EX instruction
rows.explanation: Executing instruction, or held behind a read wait. P2/P3/P7.

rows.name: MEM + WB instruction
rows.explanation: req/ret are request/completion of the SAME load, not two instructions. P5/P6.

rows.name: stall_read_i
rows.explanation: Chosen one-column data-read wait; pipeline holds. Load commits only on return. P1/P5/P6.

rows.name: branch_taken
rows.explanation: H taken in EX; G at 10 NOT taken. Wrong-path redirects suppressed. P5.

rows.name: squash_EX tags [1:0]
rows.explanation: Semantic younger-instruction tags corresponding to P1 first/second squash. Raw alignment ambiguous.

rows.name: squash_WB
rows.explanation: Semantic squash qualifier disables J/K WB effects. Annotation, not an additional drawn FF.

rows.name: ALU operand 1
rows.explanation: Consumed EX operand 1. — for held/squashed work. P3/P4.

rows.name: ALU operand 2
rows.explanation: EX register/immediate; store offset is NOT payload. Separate store payload assumed. P3.

rows.name: rs1_select
rows.explanation: EX operand source register. x0 forced to zero. P4.

rows.name: rs2_select
rows.explanation: Second source or store-payload register; immediate instructions have no consumed rs2. P4.

rows.name: fwd_sel1
rows.explanation: WB-to-EX forwarding: A→B, C→D, M→N. P4; EX reads assumed.

rows.name: fwd_sel2
rows.explanation: WB-to-EX source 2/store forwarding: A→B, D→E, N→O. P4.

rows.name: m_ext_EX
rows.explanation: F is MUL. ALU mux input 4; chosen one-clock multiplier, no DIV stall. P7a/P7c.

rows.name: wb_write_en
rows.explanation: Qualified architectural register write; zero for load request/stores/branches/squash. P4/P6.

rows.name: wb_dest_reg_sel
rows.explanation: Destination when write enabled; zero here means no write.

rows.name: wb_result
rows.explanation: Consumed ALU/MUL/load write-back value. P6.

rows.name: d_we / store_en
rows.explanation: Actual WB write pulse. Squashed J cannot write; read wait cannot repeat a store. P6/Fig 2a.

rows.name: d_addr
rows.explanation: Data/MMIO byte address held across load response; store effective address distinct from payload. P5/Fig 2a.

rows.name: d_wdata
rows.explanation: Lane-replicated payload; SB drives 0x10101010 but writes only enabled byte. P6.

rows.name: d_wstrb [3:0]
rows.explanation: Data-memory byte enables; MMIO ignores strobes and requires word access. P6/Fig 2a.

rows.name: cs_in
rows.explanation: Input peripheral address selected; selection does not imply a write. Fig 2a.

rows.name: cs_in_q
rows.explanation: One-clock registered input select; only column 17 response is consumed. Fig 2b.

rows.name: wr_en_tmr
rows.explanation: Timer selection AND d_we; L triggers both special channels with 0xA. Figs 2a/4.

rows.name: wr_en_spr
rows.explanation: Sprite selection AND d_we; S clears bullet 0, W updates P1 position. Figs 2a/5.

notes: Initial test state: x10=0x100; x11=0x80000000; RAM[0x100]=32; P1_INPUT=0x10. Other consumed initial registers = 0.
H is BEQ at PC 28 → PC 64. J/K must never commit. Independent illustrative sequence, not the real game software.

name: 02_rv32m
title: B. RV32M — normal division and immediate special-case bypass
subtitle: 24 visible columns; clocks 9–28 OMITTED (20 genuine busy clocks). Normal DIV requires 32 iterations; real elapsed time exceeds 30.

rows.name: EX operation
rows.explanation: MIN = signed 0x80000000. Special cases bypass iteration. P7b.

rows.name: fetch_pc
rows.explanation: PC held until done then increments. P7c hold convention.

rows.name: start
rows.explanation: Pulse loads abs(dividend)=100 and clears remainder before BUSY. P7b.

rows.name: busy
rows.explanation: High during 32 real iteration columns 1–32; special cases never BUSY. P7b.

rows.name: cnt_q [4:0]
rows.explanation: Iteration index 0–31. Omitted clocks contain indices 8–27. P7b.

rows.name: last_cycle
rows.explanation: cnt_q=31 during column 32; final iteration completes on next edge. P7b.

rows.name: done
rows.explanation: Normal registered completion at 33; immediate bypass for zero/overflow. P7b.

rows.name: pipeline_stall
rows.explanation: is_div_op AND NOT done. High at start and BUSY; freezes PC/IF/ID/EX. P7b/P7c.

rows.name: div_by_zero
rows.explanation: DIV gives all ones; REM gives dividend. No trap. P7b.

rows.name: overflow
rows.explanation: Signed MIN/-1: DIV gives MIN, REM gives zero. Not an exception. P7b.

rows.name: m_result
rows.explanation: Selected result; normal signed quotient truncates toward zero. P7b/P7c.

rows.name: reg_write_to_WB
rows.explanation: Enabled only when done. Busy columns insert no-write bubbles. P7c.

rows.name: wb_write_en
rows.explanation: Single commit one clock after result capture, no repeated busy write. P4/P6.

rows.name: wb_result
rows.explanation: Committed results. Normal REM -100/7 would use same stall and return -2.

notes: Start column 0; 32 iterations columns 1…32; done 33; WB 34. The // break omits clocks, not work.
DIVU/REMU have same handshake without signed correction. MUL high/low variants use funct3 without divider stall.

name: 03_collisions
title: C. Collision engine and software response — 28 continuous clocks
subtitle: Preloaded bullets and maze; arbitrary test position updates. Wall scan, inactive suppression, normal/special tank hit, bullet pair, sticky clear priority.

rows.name: scan_q [2:0]
rows.explanation: Free-running selected bullet slot 0–7. Fig 6b.

rows.name: scan_d [2:0]
rows.explanation: Slot identity delayed two clocks to match address register plus maze BRAM. Fig 6b.

rows.name: tile (wall port)
rows.explanation: Two-clock centre-tile result; 0=floor, 1=wall. Slot7 is in a wall but inactive. Fig 6b/7.

rows.name: act_d
rows.explanation: Sampled activity delayed two clocks. Inactive wall slot7 cannot set a hit. Fig 6b.

rows.name: wall_set [7:0]
rows.explanation: One-hot mask when delayed slot is active and tile nonzero. Slots0 set at 2 and 10. Fig 6b.

rows.name: b0_act
rows.explanation: Bullet0 remains alive through reflection; hardware does not remove it on wall hit. Fig 5.

rows.name: b3_act
rows.explanation: Normal bullet3 removed by a software register write at 10, effective 11. Fig 5.

rows.name: b4_act
rows.explanation: Special bullet4 removed by write at 23, effective 24. Fig 5.

rows.name: btk_hit [7:0]
rows.explanation: Live AABB hits: bullet3→P2, later bullet4→P1. Normal=6×6; special=12×12. Figs 6a/6c.

rows.name: tank_set [1:0]
rows.explanation: P1 bit0/P2 bit1. Both tanks always collision-active; no ownership filter. Fig 6c.

rows.name: bb_hit [7:0]
rows.explanation: Overlap of active bullets1/2 sets BOTH bits (0x06). Deactivating either stops the live overlap. Fig 6c.

rows.name: WALL_MASK
rows.explanation: Sticky per-bullet wall mask; persists after detection. Cleared at 5 and 14. Fig 6d.

rows.name: BB_MASK
rows.explanation: Sticky bullet-pair mask. Simultaneous clear/set at 16 clears; persistent overlap sets again at 18. Fig 6d.

rows.name: HIT_MASK
rows.explanation: Sticky {tank[1:0],bullet[7:0]}. Clear at 8 wins; still-live hit re-sets at 10. Later 0x110 identifies special bullet4/P1. Fig 6d.

rows.name: COLLISION_FLAG [2:0]
rows.explanation: bit0 any wall; bit1 any BB; bit2 any bullet-tank. ORs of sticky masks, NOT single-clock hit pulses. Fig 6d.

rows.name: wr_en_col
rows.explanation: Selected collision W1C MMIO write. Clear priority shown at 8 and 16. Fig 6d.

rows.name: clear address (offset)
rows.explanation: MMIO low offset; full base is 0x80000000. Fig 2a/6d.

rows.name: clear d_wdata
rows.explanation: Written one bits clear corresponding sticky bits; zeros do nothing. Fig 6d.

rows.name: sw.sprite write
rows.explanation: Illustrative software commits, not collision outputs. Precomputed CPU actions; actual C latency unspecified. Fig 1/5.

rows.name: sw.velocity b0
rows.explanation: SOFTWARE STATE, not a drawn FPGA port. Example vertical-wall reflection flips vx at the position-update edge.

rows.name: sw.health write
rows.explanation: Illustrative CPU HEALTH_BAR_REG writes: normal damage 1, special damage 5. Hardware only stores the requested word. Fig 1/5.

rows.name: hp1 / hp2
rows.explanation: Registered health values after CPU writes; no hardware health decrement occurs. Fig 5/12.

notes: All masks initially zero; maze and bullets already initialized. No reset is asserted in this independent continuous window.
Scan slot0 at 0 → wall_set at 2 → sticky mask at 3. After position write at 13, slot0 scan16 returns floor18.
At 8/16 clear wins over a still-live hit; deactivation or separation must precede the final acknowledgement to avoid re-latching.
Travel/reflection inputs are test stimulus. No claim that a bullet traverses a maze, or software performs all these calculations, in 28 clocks.

name: 04_input_timers
title: D. Button conditioning, cooldown trigger and expiry — 28 visible columns
subtitle: Independent windows separated by //: debounce terminal D; release terminal R; timer trigger T; long cooldown expiry E. 50 MHz assumption.

rows.name: btn_i (SHOOT)
rows.explanation: Async physical button. Initial bounce is rejected. Button sampled between edges; no metastability simulated. Fig 3.

rows.name: sync1_q
rows.explanation: First synchronizer flip-flop, one edge after sampled raw input. Fig 3.

rows.name: sync2_q
rows.explanation: Second synchronizer flip-flop, one further edge later. Fig 3.

rows.name: diff
rows.explanation: sync2_q XOR stable_q; counter resets whenever input returns to accepted level. Fig 3.

rows.name: debounce cnt_q
rows.explanation: M=DEBOUNCE_MAX=500000 at 50 MHz. Terminal comparator reads current count; stable changes on following edge. Fig 3.

rows.name: debounce done
rows.explanation: Current count equals M. One pulse at press/release endpoint; not a shoot-command pulse. Fig 3.

rows.name: stable_q
rows.explanation: Accepted level, not edge event. Press accepted D+1; release R+1. Software detects an edge by comparing polls. Fig 3.

rows.name: P1_INPUT [5:0]
rows.explanation: SHOOT is packed bit4; all other stimulus buttons zero. P2 input held zero. Fig 3.

rows.name: cs_in
rows.explanation: Read selection held across response while polling the accepted press. Fig 2a.

rows.name: cs_in_q
rows.explanation: One-clock registered read select in the shown input window; last held select continues into omitted time. Fig 2b.

rows.name: d_rdata (consumed)
rows.explanation: Input load response consumed at D+2; low word address held through read. Figs 2b/3.

rows.name: tick (1 ms)
rows.explanation: Terminal prescaler pulse, real ticks separated by 50000 clocks. T0 exercises simultaneous tick/trigger; E is an independent terminal-counter test. Fig 4.

rows.name: trig_p1_shoot
rows.explanation: T0 triggers shoot and special; T3 deliberately retriggers shoot while not ready. Hardware does not gate trigger by ready. Fig 4.

rows.name: trig_p1_spec
rows.explanation: T0 starts 20-second special cooldown. Trigger takes priority over tick/decrement. Fig 4.

rows.name: cd_cnt shoot
rows.explanation: 15-bit channel reload = 500 ms; holds without tick; nonzero counter decrements on tick. Fig 4.

rows.name: cd_cnt special
rows.explanation: 15-bit special channel reload = 20000 ms. E window jumps to final remaining millisecond. Fig 4.

rows.name: ready_p1_shoot
rows.explanation: High exactly when shoot counter zero. Counter does not underflow. Fig 4.

rows.name: ready_p1_spec
rows.explanation: High exactly when special counter zero. P2 channels idle/ready throughout. Fig 4.

rows.name: TIMER_STATUS [3:0]
rows.explanation: bit0 P1 shoot, bit1 P1 special, bit2 P2 shoot, bit3 P2 special. Fig 4.

notes: Debounce gaps hide about 10 ms of sustained mismatch on each transition; M+1 column follows literal current-count comparator timing.
T0 coincides with a real terminal tick: trigger wins over decrement. E is an independent endpoint test with both counters initially 1; not a simultaneous expiry claim.
Normal software must check ready before shooting; hardware reloads even a busy channel if software writes a trigger. No FPGA fire-request pulse is drawn.

name: 05_pixel_mixer
title: E. Display pixel priority and blanking — 28 continuous clocks
subtitle: Aligned Fig 10 input test: HUD > big bullet > normal bullet > tank > wall > background. Final RGB registered once.

rows.name: active_d
rows.explanation: Delayed active qualifier at mixer input. Low blanks RGB regardless of layer valids. Fig 10.

rows.name: maze_wall
rows.explanation: Aligned wall valid. Floor RGB computed by Fig 11 does not override BG in the pictured mixer. Figs 10/11.

rows.name: tank_valid
rows.explanation: Combined tank valid after sprite ROM/combining register. Fig 9; input alignment assumed.

rows.name: tank_valid_P2
rows.explanation: Both tanks hit the test pixel: P2 wins colour selection. Supplied as aligned test stimulus. Fig 9.

rows.name: bullet_valid
rows.explanation: Normal bullet pixel valid overrides tank/wall. Figs 9/10.

rows.name: big_valid
rows.explanation: Special bullet pixel valid overrides normal bullet. Figs 9/10.

rows.name: hud_valid
rows.explanation: Heart shape pixel has highest priority. Full and empty hearts both valid; health changes colour only. Figs 10/12.

rows.name: hud_rgb
rows.explanation: Full red then empty grey heart test pixels; prealigned colour. Fig 12.

rows.name: tank_rgb
rows.explanation: P1 green then P2 blue on overlapping masks. Fig 9.

rows.name: selected layer
rows.explanation: Diagnostic annotation for combinational priority; not an extra hardware bus. Fig 10.

rows.name: pixel RGB (pre-FF)
rows.explanation: 12-bit value after blank mux, hex RGB444. Fig 10.

rows.name: vga_rgb_q
rows.explanation: One-clock registered output. active_d low at 24 → RGB black at 25. Fig 10.

notes: Overlapping valid streams prove priority without claiming a fast full-screen scan. This is a mixer-input test.
Transparent ROM pixels have valid=0 and reveal lower layers. Actual shape ROM bits are not specified in the block diagrams.

name: 06_vga_horizontal
title: F. VGA horizontal boundaries — visible blank, HS low, HS high, line wrap
subtitle: Four independent seven-clock windows; // separates preconditioned boundary tests. 50 MHz clk_sys, alternating 25 MHz pix_ce.

rows.name: pix_ce
rows.explanation: Counter enable, not a clock. Only enabled edges advance counters. Fig 8.

rows.name: hcnt_q / x
rows.explanation: Horizontal counter 0–799; held on disabled pixel clocks. Fig 8.

rows.name: vcnt_q / y
rows.explanation: Vertical counter advances on line_tick only; 524→0 at frame wrap. Fig 8.

rows.name: h_end
rows.explanation: Current horizontal count equals 799; may span two clocks. Fig 8.

rows.name: v_end
rows.explanation: Current vertical count equals 524; requires line_tick for frame wrap. Fig 8.

rows.name: line_tick
rows.explanation: pix_ce AND h_end; advances vertical counter once per line. Fig 8.

rows.name: active_q
rows.explanation: Registered visible test h<640 AND v<480. Fig 8.

rows.name: hs_win_q
rows.explanation: Positive registered 656<=h<752 window; one chosen consistent polarity. Figs 8/10.

rows.name: vs_win_q
rows.explanation: Positive registered 490<=v<492 window. Figs 8/10.

rows.name: active_d
rows.explanation: Literal three-FF delay of active_q before blank mux. Fig 10.

rows.name: hsync_n
rows.explanation: NOT hs_win_q delayed three clocks, exactly one inversion. Fig 10.

rows.name: vsync_n
rows.explanation: NOT vs_win_q delayed three clocks, exactly one inversion. Fig 10.

rows.name: vga_rgb_q
rows.explanation: RGB register consumes active_d one further clock later; steady nonblank test colour 888. Fig 10.

notes: Sync pin changes five displayed clocks after window start; RGB blank change follows one clock later under literal Fig 10.
Each window has steady prehistory. // does not skip required counter values within a single continuous trace.
Exact coordinate-to-output alignment is NOT established by these conflicting drawings; verify/reset RTL before relying on pin timing.

rows.name: hcnt_q / x

name: 08_memory_render
title: H. Maze coherence, tile boundary, sprite ROM and health HUD — 28 visible columns
subtitle: Independent windows: mirrored maze write/read | 24-pixel tile crossing | bullet visibility | HUD heart valid/colour. No same-address read/write collision tested.

rows.name: wr_en_maze
rows.explanation: CPU maze write decode. Chosen tile5 address is in range. Fig 2a/7.

rows.name: we_cpu (V and C)
rows.explanation: Single range-qualified pulse drives BOTH maze copies. CPU is not stalled by independent read ports. Fig 7.

rows.name: CPU maze address
rows.explanation: Tile5 address = 0x80000100+4×5. Held for read at 2/3. Fig 7.

rows.name: CPU maze wdata
rows.explanation: Low two bits written: 2=breakable wall. Both copies update at right edge of column0. Fig 7.

rows.name: RAM V[5] / C[5]
rows.explanation: Mirrored stored tile contents; initialized floor then coherent update to breakable. Diagnostic memory-state annotation. Fig 7.

rows.name: cs_maze
rows.explanation: CPU read selects maze; only write pulse at0 alters copies. Fig 2a.

rows.name: cs_maze_q
rows.explanation: One-clock registered select; response consumed at3. Fig 2b.

rows.name: CPU d_rdata
rows.explanation: One-clock CPU BRAM read, zero-extended tile. Low address held through response. Fig 7/2b.

rows.name: VGA / collision addr
rows.explanation: Independent read ports both request tile5 after write completed; no arbitration. Fig 7.

rows.name: VGA / collision data
rows.explanation: Synchronous read data one clock after port addresses. Concurrent same-address write/read behaviour is NOT specified. Fig 7.

rows.name: pix_ce
rows.explanation: Tile test uses alternating enabled pixel edges at 50 MHz. Fig 8/11.

rows.name: pixel x
rows.explanation: Coordinate crosses 24-pixel tile boundary, y fixed0; disabled clocks hold. Fig 11.

rows.name: sub_x / tile_col
rows.explanation: Tile subcounter wraps23→0 and column advances at the same edge as x. Fig 11.

rows.name: vga_tile_addr
rows.explanation: row×20+col. Boundary test tile0=floor, tile1=wall; no division hardware. Fig 11.

rows.name: vga_tile_data
rows.explanation: Tile RAM returns preceding column address. Independent window has floor prehistory. Fig 7.

rows.name: maze_wall_q
rows.explanation: Registered nonzero tile AND in_field_d. RAM then output FF gives two-clock coordinate-to-wall delay. Fig 11.

rows.name: maze_rgb_q
rows.explanation: Floor/wall stream colours. Floor222 is NOT selected as BG by literal Fig10. Fig 11.

rows.name: bullet in_box
rows.explanation: Bullet pixel bounding-box hit before FF; illustrative ROM shape=1 at these addresses. Fig 9.

rows.name: bullet act
rows.explanation: Source register alive until software clear effective at16. Delayed act must suppress ROM output. Fig 9.

rows.name: in_box_d / shape
rows.explanation: Bounding-box FF and synchronous shape ROM both delayed one clock. Shape stimulus chosen, not derived from absent ROM contents. Fig 9.

rows.name: sprite act_d
rows.explanation: Alive FF delayed one clock. act source cleared16 → act_d low17. Fig 9.

rows.name: bN_small_hit
rows.explanation: ROM shape AND delayed box AND delayed activity, normal bullet mode. Fig 9.

rows.name: bullet_valid (combined)
rows.explanation: Additional combined output FF mentioned in Fig9 PartC; one clock after small_hit. Alignment with other sources is assumed.

rows.name: HUD slot / hp
rows.explanation: slot<hp gives full heart. Slot19 empty when hp19; geometry within HUD strip. Fig 12.

rows.name: HUD in_hud
rows.explanation: Inside HUD row and strip. Independent illustrative pixel inputs; not a consecutive raster coordinate sweep. Fig 12.

rows.name: HUD lit_d
rows.explanation: One-clock registered slot<hp. Initial full prehistory, then empty slot accepted23. Fig 12.

rows.name: HUD shape (ROM)
rows.explanation: Chosen synchronous heart ROM bit=1; last shape output remains for one clock after leaving region. Fig 12.

rows.name: hud_valid_q
rows.explanation: Registered in_hud_d AND shape, two clocks after geometry. Empty hearts remain valid. Fig 12.

rows.name: hud_rgb_q
rows.explanation: Final HUD colour FF consumes lit_d; independent of shape validity. Fig 12.

notes: ROM outputs use illustrative shape bits since block diagrams contain no ROM image data. Streams are independent diagnostic tests.
RAM same-address cross-port write/read mode and RAM reset contents are unspecified; this test avoids that collision and assumes preloaded tiles.
Unqualified X tile restart at h_end in Fig11 must be checked when pix_ce=0; boundary tests use a qualified restart convention.

name: 09_cpu_corner_cases
title: I. CPU corner cases — loads, halfword lanes, x0, jump and exception detect
subtitle: Seven independent four-clock tests; // separates transactions. Valid inputs established before window. Trap/recovery not specified by diagrams.

rows.name: WB transaction
rows.explanation: Independent transactions through load/store/control blocks. P2/P5/P6.

rows.name: stall_read_i
rows.explanation: Chosen initial read wait only for load tests. Return qualified once next clock. P6 assumption.

rows.name: wb_read_data
rows.explanation: Test BRAM word; byte1=0x80, halfword1=0x8000. P6.

rows.name: wb_write_en
rows.explanation: Qualified writes; write x0 request may assert, but reads remain forced zero. Architectural x0 protection needs implementation check. P4.

rows.name: wb_result
rows.explanation: LB/LH sign extension versus LBU/LHU zero extension. x0 attempted data99 does not change x0 read result. P6/P4.

rows.name: d_we / store_en
rows.explanation: SH transaction pulse; no load peripheral write. P6.

rows.name: d_addr
rows.explanation: Aligned halfword at upper pair of word0x100. Misaligned access/trap behaviour unspecified. P6.

rows.name: d_wdata
rows.explanation: Halfword0xABCD replicated twice by store-data mux. P6.

rows.name: d_wstrb
rows.explanation: SH upper pair at addr[1]=1. Lower SH uses0011; SB uses0001/0010/0100/1000; SW1111. P6.

rows.name: zero1 / zero2
rows.explanation: Both source addresses0 force both read operands0, overriding even matching WB forwarding. P4.

rows.name: reg_rdata1 / 2
rows.explanation: Consumed x0 read-port values; x0 is architecturally zero. P4.

rows.name: branch_taken
rows.explanation: JALR redirect unconditional. No target instruction retirement shown in this isolated comparator test. P5.

rows.name: fetch_pc_o (JALR)
rows.explanation: rs1=201, immediate0 → target (201+0)&~1=200. JALR clears low bit. P5.

rows.name: reset_n
rows.explanation: Exception test reset qualifier. CPU reset/hold/squash priority not determined by this isolated equation test. P2.

rows.name: illegal_inst
rows.explanation: Explicit decoder illegal input stimulus; suppressed by reset_n=0 at26. P2.

rows.name: instruction_i == 0
rows.explanation: All-zero instruction also contributes to exception detect. A legal NOP0x13 does NOT. P2.

rows.name: exception
rows.explanation: (illegal_inst OR instruction_i==0) AND reset_n as drawn. Trap PC/cause/recovery outputs absent; no invented trap sequence. P2.

notes: Aligned data-memory tests only. MMIO is word-only; SB/SH MMIO behaviour should not be inferred from data-memory lane tests.
Normal ALU add/shift/logic/compare are selected combinationally; numeric examples in sheet A cover ADD, MUL, SLT, OR, LUI, SRAI and XOR.
